text:
arjun: Heads-up — noticed an uptick in ECC / Xid errors in eu-west-1 over the last 24h. ~12 distinct GPU cards flagged, most on older A100-40GB hosts. Creating a thread to agree spare-pool sizing and replacement window.

sasha: Do we have a failure rate (normalized) rather than raw counts? and are these correctable vs hard-failures?

maria: Metric dump: 12 cards with ECC/Xid events in 24h out of ~2200 GPUs in eu-west-1 → ~0.55%/day. Mix is ~60% correctable ECC single-bit, 40% driver-reset Xid (some lead to node drain). Pattern: spike after sustained high p99 token/sec runs. Logs: 

```
# sample audit snippet
2026-03-16T03:21:12Z node-az3-472 ECC error: Correctable single-bit
2026-03-16T05:02:01Z node-az3-479 Xid 13 GPU fault, driver reset
2026-03-16T06:15:44Z node-az2-101 flapping MIG profile detachment
```

cj: If baseline is 0.55%/day that's ~12/day. For spare sizing we should think in terms of a replacement window (how long it takes to detect, drain, ship, and replace). For hardware replacements we use W = 3 days operationally.

sasha: Quick sizing calc (pooled region):

```
cards_total = 2200
failures_per_day = 12  # observed
replacement_window_days = 3
expected_failures = failures_per_day * replacement_window_days  # 36
safety_factor = 1.3  # accounts for burstiness + detection lag
spare_needed = ceil(expected_failures * safety_factor)  # 47
spare_pct = spare_needed / cards_total  # ~2.1%
```

sasha: So strictly by this calc we need ~47 spare GPUs (~2.1%). But this assumes failures are independent and Poisson-ish — they are not (we've seen bursts). I recommend targetting 4-6% as an operational buffer for eu-west-1 while we root-cause.

ops-lead: We need to balance cost. 5% of 2200 = 110 GPUs reserved. We can use a mix: 30 GPUs hot spare (immediate), 80 GPUs opportunistic (burst capacity / preemptible contracts) to keep cost down.

maria: Cost sketch: if hot-spare is on reserved nodes there is a monthly delta. If we instead reserve burst quota with provider, we pay only when used. Suggest: short-term (2 weeks) keep 5% effective spare via burst+hot-spare.

cj: Also consider traffic shaping: reduce low-priority background workloads when spare pool < 2x expected replacement rate. We can add a dynamic autoscale policy. Example patch for policy service: 

```
PATCH /api/v1/policies/scale HTTP/1.1
Content-Type: application/json
{
  "name": "eu-west-spare-guard",
  "threshold": {"spare_pct": 0.02},
  "action": {"deprioritize": ["batch-embedding", "background-eval"]}
}
```

sasha: Also - short-term mitigation: roll GPU driver to 525.89 which we saw reduce Xid resets in canary by ~70%. If that holds, failure_rate should drop to ~0.15%/day -> spare need becomes much smaller. Schedule: roll canary today; full roll Monday.

oncall-bot: Incident created: GPU_ECC_SPIKE_EUW1 (INC-2026-0316-01). Runbook: https://redwood.internal/runbooks/gpu-failure-triage

ops-lead: Proposed immediate actions: 
- increase effective spare target for eu-west-1 to 5% (mix hot + burst) for 14 days
- run driver rollback canary today, rollback group if metric improves
- enable autoscale policy to deprioritize batch when spare_pct < 2%
- start 3-day replacement workflow for the 12 flagged nodes (ticket ops/infra#4221)

maria: I'll post cost delta + procurement note by EOD.

arjun: +1. Also capture per-az breakdown and update the spare-allocation across AZs (we should avoid all spares in one AZ).

sasha: Action owners: 
- maria -> cost/procure plan (EOD)
- ops-lead -> implement hot/burst config + create reservation (4h)
- cj -> autoscale policy patch (tomorrow)
- arjun -> coordinate driver canary (today)

arjun: Thanks everyone — will reconvene in 24h with canary numbers. :white_check_mark:
